title: Generic 'unable to charge' error
shortDescription: Station displays a non-specific charging failure.
fullDescription:
ChargePoint Home Flex and CT4000 commercial stations display this error when a session fails to start for multiple possible reasons. The ChargePoint app typically provides a more specific sub-code.

Check the app first, then power cycle, then contact support with the station serial number.

fixSteps.title: Check app for detail
fixSteps.instruction: Open ChargePoint app → station → see specific reason.

fixSteps.title: Contact support
fixSteps.instruction: Call ChargePoint with serial number if issue persists.

whenToCallPro: If power cycle does not resolve.

faq.a: On label inside faceplate or in app.

title: RFID card not recognized
shortDescription: Station cannot read the RFID membership card.
fullDescription:
ChargePoint stations use RFID cards to authenticate drivers. If the card is demagnetized, the station is offline (can't query backend), or the card isn't linked to an active account, the station refuses to start.

Use the app to start charging if the card fails.

fixSteps.title: Start via app
fixSteps.instruction: Use ChargePoint app to scan the QR and start the session.

fixSteps.title: Verify card
fixSteps.instruction: In app → Payments → RFID cards — confirm card is active.

faq.q: Is there a replacement card fee?
faq.a: First card is free; replacements may cost $5.

title: Station has no cellular signal
fullDescription:
Commercial CT4000 stations use cellular (AT&T) to talk to ChargePoint cloud. Without signal, RFID cards can't be verified. In OCPP configurations, local authorization lists may still work.

Check AT&T coverage at the site; in basements a cellular booster may be needed.

fixSteps.title: Check app map
fixSteps.instruction: Other stations also offline? Likely carrier outage.

fixSteps.title: Signal booster
fixSteps.instruction: Install a cellular booster if coverage is chronically weak.

title: Connector will not release from vehicle
shortDescription: J1772 or NACS connector stuck in the car.
fullDescription:
After charging, the car should unlock and allow the connector to pull free. If it stays locked, either the car hasn't unlocked (try unlocking doors) or the charger hasn't sent the end-session signal.

Lock/unlock the car with the key fob to release.
whenToCallPro: If the latch is mechanically jammed.

faq.a: Many cars have manual release in frunk or service manual.

title: Internal power module failure
shortDescription: Charger's contactor or power electronics failed.
fullDescription: A power module fault is internal and requires service. The station reports the fault to ChargePoint operations who dispatch technicians. For Home Flex, it's a unit replacement under warranty.

fixSteps.title: Contact ChargePoint
fixSteps.instruction: Call 877-370-3802 with station serial for warranty service.

title: Authorization failed
shortDescription: Driver could not be authorized to charge.
fullDescription: Auth failure can mean declined payment, expired membership, or a backend account issue. The station cannot start the session until auth clears.

title: Station running in offline mode
shortDescription: Station lost backend connection — limited functionality.
fullDescription:
When the station cannot reach ChargePoint cloud, it enters offline mode. Some RFID cards stored locally may still work, but new drivers cannot start a session.

Billing resumes when the station is back online.

fixSteps.title: Check site network
fixSteps.instruction: Confirm building internet or cellular coverage.

whenToCallPro: If network is fine but station stays offline.

faq.a: New drivers yes; known RFID often works.

title: Billing or session record error
shortDescription: Session could not be billed or recorded.
fullDescription: Billing errors appear when the cloud backend has trouble reconciling a session. It does not affect charging — driver still gets power. The charge is reconciled later.

fixSteps.title: Contact support
fixSteps.instruction: If still an error, call for manual reconciliation.

title: Station kicker module error
fullDescription:
The 'kicker' is a small inrush-limiting module inside CT4000 that charges capacitors gradually at power-up. If it fails, the main contactor never closes and the station stays dead.

Requires ChargePoint technician to replace.

fixSteps.title: Contact ChargePoint
fixSteps.instruction: Open warranty case for kicker replacement.

faq.a: Try one breaker cycle; if no change, service required.

title: Charging slower than expected
shortDescription: Charger delivers less power than rated.
fullDescription:
Home Flex outputs up to 50A. If you see lower, causes include: breaker set lower in commissioning, car onboard charger limit (e.g., 32A Leaf), station throttling due to heat, or load sharing with another station.

Check configured amps in app; match to breaker.

fixSteps.title: Check amps config
fixSteps.instruction: App → Station settings → Max current; match your breaker (40A for 50A breaker).

fixSteps.title: Verify car limit
fixSteps.instruction: Check vehicle onboard charger spec — many are 32A or 40A max.
